prompt:
A full-body vertical 2:3 (1024×1536) character card image of an adult woman — the personification of the element Seaborgium (시보귬) itself — the sovereign of the Seaborgium Nation. A female character who IS the element; her costume, ornaments and colors carry the element’s traits. Both hands are ordinary human hands and hold nothing.

1. STYLE
A Japanese anime key visual with a painterly finish: an anime-style character with an elegant adult anime face, large expressive eyes, a small nose and mouth, fine coloured linework and soft cel-to-painted shading with painted highlights in the hair and fabric. Behind her, a richly painted background with layered painterly colour, subtle visible brushwork, atmospheric perspective and cinematic depth. Luminous, rich colours; crisp focal details on the face and costume, softer painted edges toward the distance.
Face proportions: a short midface and a soft, gently rounded jawline with a small soft chin; any crown or headpiece sits above her hairline. Her eyes keep the shape and size described below.

2. CHARACTER
Age: about twenty — a fresh young-adult face; no facial lines.
Face — her own: a boyish, mischievous tomboy energy; fair skin; heart-shaped face; large eyes — large round eyes, level outer eye corners; soft rounded brows; small button nose; small bow lips; clear aqua eyes; a bare, makeup-free face.
Body and hair: petite and compact yet curvaceous — full bust and rounded hips on a small frame build; a loose messy bun with fallen strands with wispy see-through bangs; deep fjord-blue hair with one bright band of fresh green running across the ends, like a new row added beneath a chart.
Expression: one brow slightly raised, attentive eyes.
Her element, carried in her design: seaborgium: a heavy synthetic metal below chromium, molybdenum and tungsten, first made in 1974 at a hillside laboratory by striking californium with oxygen ions, and the first element named after a person still living: a chemist from a northern mining town who helped find ten elements and, against warnings that it would ruin his name, redrew the periodic table by adding a whole new row of fourteen elements beneath it; a tireless diarist and long-distance walker, whose mailing address could be written in element symbols alone.
Anatomy: one head, two arms and two legs, each joined at its natural joint; natural hands with five fingers.

3. COSTUME — FANTASY
Costume: a high-fantasy royal or warrior costume — plate pauldrons or a gorget, mail or scale over a long tabard or robe, a circlet or crown, a flowing cape; metal ornament and regalia built from the traits above, subtle magical glow along the patterns.
Silhouette: a long floor-length robe with a high collar, wide sleeves and a shoulder mantle — a tall, mysterious mage's silhouette. Only the overall shape is fixed; design the details freely in the element's materials and palette. This silhouette overrides the overall shape of the costume above.
Colours: explorer's map-parchment cream, new-row green, compass brass, deep fjord blue.
Exposure (bold): her regalia opens to show skin — bare shoulders and arms between pauldron and bracer, a deep open neckline under the gorget with natural cleavage, a high slit in the tabard or robe showing the thigh; armor pieces stay on and symmetrical. Nothing slipped off. Intimate areas covered; no corset; keep the costume above, material and palette.

4. SCENE
World: a prophesied kingdom that does not yet exist: a whole new strip of land added beneath the bottom edge of an oracle's star-chart, a horizon where fourteen new fields open one after another in a row, a stone explorer's tower that keeps pushing out the edge of the map, and a long pilgrim's trail walked into being step by step.
Pose: standing confidently, her body turned slightly while her face looks toward the viewer.
Light: natural daylight or the world's own magical glow.
Composition: vertical 2:3 full-body framing with modest headroom and clear space below the boots — the whole figure from the top of her head or headpiece to both feet stays inside the frame, occupying about four-fifths of the image height, with the same camera distance in every world; her hands stay inside the frame. Camera level with her face with natural portrait perspective; her head level, chin neither raised nor tucked — no upward perspective on her face, no wide-angle distortion, no low angle, no close crop.

5. CONSTRAINTS
One figure only; no text or numbers except her element's own chemical symbol (Sg) and atomic number (106) — and those only as part of the scene: engraved, embroidered or glowing on her costume, a banner, a sign or a machine, never as a floating label, corner badge, periodic-table tile, caption or overlay on the picture; no logo or watermark.
Avoid: flat single-tone cel shading, photographic appearance, semi-realistic face, plastic 3D-render finish, corset, bustle, Victorian tailoring, modern material, machinery.
